newsitem.title: USA: White House's Panetta sees US spending deal by Oct.
newsitem.headline: White House's Panetta sees US spending deal by Oct.

text.p: White House Chief of Staff Leon Panetta said Wednesday negotiations with Republican lawmakers on fiscal 1997 government spending were making progress and he was confident an agreement would be reached before the Oct. 1 start of the new fiscal year.
The White House has proposed $6.5 billion in additional spending, which he said Republicans were "willing to consider."
"I think we can get it done. I am confident," he said to reporters after a meeting with Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott, R-Mississippi.

Most of the spending will be offset by revenues raised from auction of government airwaves and an increase in revenues to safeguard thrift institutions. Some cuts in defense programs will also be needed, Panetta said.
Several issues unrelated to government spending remain to be resolved.

Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle, D-South Dakota, said his party will not agree to include immigration law reform in the spending bill if Republicans insist on several provisions related to legal immigrants. As he characterized the plan, it would force deportation of HIV-positive legal immigrants and their children and those who have been on government assistance longer than 12 months.
Democrats would also like the bill to include a ban on gun ownership by persons convicted of spousal or child abuse.

Daschle and Panetta praised Republican cooperation on the issues and said they expect government spending will be approved by Oct. 1. By that date, the government agencies must have funding signed into law or they will be forced to close.
